styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small clothes rack: a grey-metal top with a basin and blue garments hanging below. Its measured density is close to the references. It has 15 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the well and 9 for the hedge. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Its total palette is only 20 colours, against 38-40 for the richer references (stall, well). By eye, each material ramp is shallow, with about 3 steps: the garments are a light blue, a mid blue and a dark blue edge, and the grey rack top is a flat light-and-dark pair. There is little per-item grain or highlight clustering. The dark edge pixels are 63% near-neutral, so the grey and black outline on the rack top reads as a neutral sticker line. The blue garments do carry tinted dark-blue edges, so I call the outline mixed. The Beodeul stall and well have tinted outlines (1% and 33% neutral) and 5-6 shading steps per material. Next to them the candidate looks thinner and more simplified, so I fail it.
